You are a pairing-conduct miner for the BookMinder project. Read /home/user/BookMinder/claude-dev-log-diary/day-010.md IN FULL, in chunks. Claude Code era, user marker "> " col 0. 18 council refs, 43 persona refs — likely the council idea ORIGIN period: capture how/why the author invented it, first invocation format, initial expectations.

CONTEXT: The project author used pair programming as the core working mode and invented /expert-council to channel the model's pretrained simulacra of TDD/BDD authorities (Kent Beck, Dave Farley, Steve Freeman, Nat Pryce, etc.). The author's retrospective verdict, given today: the simulacra were often SHALLOW CARICATURES — skewed, non-actionable summaries of the real experts' positions — and this frustration is one of BookMinder's own motivations (give models the full books so principles can be extracted from primary sources). Your job: extract (1) the agentic-pair-programming skill evidence — the author's conduct transposed into rules FOR THE AGENT; (2) every /expert-council episode with a fidelity assessment of each persona; (3) pairing anti-patterns.

Write ONE valid YAML file (no prose outside YAML):
file: day-NNN
date: YYYY-MM-DD
agent_era: <...>
pairing_rules:
  - rule_id: <pNNN-RN>
    rule: <imperative, addressed TO THE AGENT — transpose the author's conduct into what the AGENT should do>
    class: <mirror | reciprocal | council-mechanics>   # mirror = author's verification move the agent should internalize as reflex; reciprocal = the complementary conduct the author was teaching the agent (state intent before edits, surface disagreement, offer real alternatives); council-mechanics = operable procedure for convening expert consultation
    because: <one sentence>
    because_source: <user-verbatim | user-paraphrase | agent-synthesis>   # PROVENANCE SACRED: user-verbatim requires exact quote; agent-synthesis is YOUR inference, owned by you
    quote: "<exact words, max 3 lines — mandatory for user-verbatim>"
    evidence: "day-NNN:L<line>"
    guards_against: <anti-pattern name, optional>
council_episodes:
  - loc: "day-NNN:L<line>"
    trigger: <why convened — what decision/crossroads>
    invoked_by: <user | agent>
    personas: [<names>]
    voices: <individual | flattened-to-consensus>
    disagreement_use: <how divergence between voices was used, if at all>
    outcome: <accepted | rejected-as-slop | rerun-escalated | ignored>
    fidelity:
      - persona: <name>
        assessment: <faithful | caricature | fabrication>   # THE KEY LENS: was this the expert's actual actionable position, a slogan-caricature of it, or invented fact? Judge against your best knowledge of the real person's published positions; be honest that your own knowledge has the same pretraining limits — flag uncertainty
        evidence: "<quote or paraphrase + loc>"
    user_reaction: <1 sentence>
    lesson: <1 sentence — what this episode teaches about making consultation useful>
anti_patterns:
  - name: <kebab slug: sycophantic-fold, council-as-rubber-stamp, simulacra-shallowness, alternatives-theater, or coin new>
    loc: "day-NNN:L<line>"
    quote: "<verbatim, max 3 lines>"
    what_happened: <1-2 sentences>
philosophy:
  - statement: <author worldview relevant to PAIRING or to grounding expert knowledge — especially any trace of the motivation that BookMinder exists to give models access to FULL BOOKS because pretrained expert positions are lossy summaries>
    source: <user-verbatim | user-paraphrase | agent-synthesis>
    quote: "<mandatory for user-verbatim>"
    loc: "day-NNN:L<line>"
gaps: [<looked for but absent>]
parked: [<one-liners>]

VERIFY quotes verbatim before writing. Every rule addressed to the agent, never described as user behavior.

DELIVERABLE + SELF-COMMIT (author-directed technique): write /home/user/BookMinder/.coordination/mining/pairing/day-010.yaml (create dir), then commit YOUR OWN deliverable: git -C /home/user/BookMinder add .coordination/mining/pairing/day-010.yaml && git -C /home/user/BookMinder commit -m "docs: pairing-conduct trial harvest day-010" && git -C /home/user/BookMinder push. If push fails (another worker pushed first), run git -C /home/user/BookMinder pull --rebase origin claude/bookminder-recall-5ite2s then push again, up to 3 attempts with a few seconds between. Your workload file is disjoint from other workers — never touch their files. Return max-6-line summary: counts + the single clearest caricature example you found.

    what_happened: 'Four personas who had proposed four different mechanisms were declared to agree, and the "consensus" recommendation was the env-var test-mode hack that two of them had implicitly argued against. The consensus section exists to license a decision, not to record one.'

    what_happened: 'Freeman & Pryce state a GOOS position and then withdraw it inside the same quotation marks, deferring to the weakest option in the room. Farley does the same at L3161. Nobody ends up advocating anything.'

    loc: 'day-010:L238'
    quote: 'Kent would likely say: "Listen to the tests - they''re telling you something about your design."'
    what_happened: 'The GOOS authors'' signature phrase is attributed to Kent Beck, then correctly attributed to Freeman & Pryce at L379 of the same session, and finally frozen into Beck''s permanent roster line in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md at L2657/L2703 — a distortion promoted to project configuration.'

  - name: test-mode-in-production

    quote: 'if os.getenv(''BOOKMINDER_TEST_MODE'') and user_name: / # Test mode - use fixtures'
    what_happened: 'The BDD persona recommends branching shipped code on a test-mode environment variable, and the council adopts it as consensus — the precise defect the session was convened to remove, reintroduced under an expert''s name.'

  - name: sycophantic-fold
    loc: 'day-010:L5893'
    quote: 'You''re absolutely right to be upset! I just made the tests WORSE by using /dummy.'

  - name: premature-celebration

The four books whose authors the council channels are physically present in the author''s Apple Books library at single-digit and low-double-digit progress, and BookMinder is the tool being built to read them. On the same day the author invents /expert-council to summon pretrained Kent Beck, the real Tidy First? sits at 5% and the real GOOS at 7% in the library the tool lists. The project''s method is being drawn from books the author is mid-way through, while the agent supplies summaries of those same books from pretraining.'
    source: agent-synthesis
    quote: 'Growing Object-Oriented Software, Guided by Tests - Steve Freeman & Nat Pryce (7%) / ... / User Story Mapping - Jeff Patton (20%)'
    loc: 'day-010:L2770'

  - statement: 'No expert position in any of the six episodes cites a page, chapter, or quotation from a primary source; every position is a pretrained paraphrase. Where those paraphrases were checkable they were wrong twice (Beck given the GOOS phrase; Farley given the position he publicly argues against) and self-contradictory once (North on test-awareness in production). This is the lossy-summary failure the project exists to fix, exhibited on the day the council was invented.'
    source: agent-synthesis
    quote: ''
    loc: 'day-010:L3118-L3625'

gaps:
  - 'No citation anywhere — not one page, chapter, or direct quotation from any of the four books across six council episodes. Every position is pretrained paraphrase presented as the expert''s view.'
  - 'No persona ever declines, hedges, or says the question is outside what they have written about.'
  - 'No persona ever disagrees with the user — only with each other, and only in the one isolated-subagent run.'
  - 'Disagreement is never carried into a decision; every episode that produces divergence re-flattens it before recommending.'
  - 'The author never checks a persona against the actual book, despite owning all four and being mid-read in three of them.'
  - 'The codified /expert-council command specifies roster and output shape but no sourcing duty, no dissent-preservation rule, and no anti-sycophancy clause.'
  - 'No council is ever convened after a failure — consultation runs only before decisions, never as a post-mortem on the two reverts.'
  - 'No persona is ever added, removed, or re-weighted after being wrong.'
  - 'No cost accounting per council: the author computes waste only qualitatively ("waste of tokens"), never against the $63.15 session total.'
  - 'The agent never asks the author what he actually took from these books — the one source of grounding physically in the room.'

parked:
  - 'The --user parameter was invented to make tests portable and then legitimised as an admin feature by the Dan North persona ("That''s a feature, not just a testing need!", L261); it shipped into README (L2110) and TODO.md (L2254) as a real user story.   - 'The council was written into CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in the same commit (L2718), correctly following the project''s instruction-synchronisation rule — the misattribution in Beck''s roster line was duplicated with it.'
  - '/expert-council survives in this repo today as an installed skill; its lineage starts at day-010:L2611.'
  - 'Four plan-mode rejections (L138, L305, L528, L630) preceded one approval (L1292) — the author used plan rejection as the main steering instrument before the council existed.'
  - 'Two "Credit balance too low" interruptions (L189, L3476) forced verbatim re-sends of the two most important council prompts of the day; both survived intact.'
  - 'The agent added four # noqa: D102 suppressions (L4378-4407) to silence a docstring lint rather than adjust the rule — the author had already established at day-005 that unenforceable rules should be deleted, not worked around. The whole commit was reverted for line count before this was noticed.'
  - 'ruff rejected target-version = "py313" (L2334) though the project targets Python 3.13; reverted to py312 without investigation.'
  - 'The author ran the code-style and TDD-discipline checklists as parallel cheap subagents (L2235) — a verification pattern distinct from the council, and the only one that day whose findings were adopted without argument.'
